treatment_rationale.summary: Tamoxifen blocks ER-driven growth in breast tissue and is an endocrine option across pre- and postmenopausal ER-positive NCCP00253 settings. Active-metabolite formation and tissue-specific effects explain interaction checks and individualized clot, uterine and bone review.
treatment_rationale.setting: Adjuvant or advanced ER-positive breast cancer within NCCP00253.
treatment_rationale.line: Adjuvant initial or extended endocrine plan; advanced therapy according to the consultant plan.
factors: Confirm ER positivity and exact setting.
Review menopause, prior endocrine treatment, recurrence risk and tolerability.
Review VTE history, uterine symptoms, eye disease, liver function and interacting medicines.
Treatment duration and switching are planned decisions, not automatic continuation.
alternatives: An aromatase inhibitor may be an alternative in an appropriate postmenopausal or ovarian-suppression plan; its bone and joint risks differ.
Choice of an advanced-disease endocrine combination depends on previous treatment, disease features and the separate regimen eligibility.
treatment_rationale.limitations: Trial benefits are population-specific; do not rank regimens across unrelated studies or infer prevention indications.

evidence_at_a_glance.trial: EBCTCG; ATLAS; supportive aTTom duration context
evidence_at_a_glance.population: ER-positive early breast cancer; initial adjuvant treatment and extension decisions are distinct.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: EBCTCG: about 5 years versus none. ATLAS/aTTom: continue to 10 years versus stop at 5 years.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: NCCP00253 also includes advanced disease; these adjuvant results do not provide a metastatic survival estimate.

endpoints.metric: ATLAS overall mortality in the ER-positive population
endpoints.interpretation: Overall mortality was lower with extended treatment in ATLAS; not a fixed-time survival percentage.
endpoints.definition: Death from any cause after randomization at completion of 5 years tamoxifen.
endpoints.limitations: Different endpoint from breast-cancer mortality; use the correct denominator and population.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: EBCTCG 2011: ER-positive recurrence rate ratios 0.53 during years 0–4 and 0.68 during years 5–9; breast-cancer mortality fell by about one-third through 15 years. ATLAS years 5–14 recurrence was 21.4% versus 25.1% and breast-cancer mortality 12.2% versus 15.0%. These are recurrence and cause-specific mortality results, not DFS or OS percentages.
limitations: Absolute benefit depends on recurrence risk.
aTTom corroborates recurrence reduction but its overall mortality comparison was not significant (P=.1); it included many ER-untested patients and is sourced here to a meeting abstract.
Extension is not automatic for everyone; benefit and harm populations in ATLAS differ.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: ATLAS: extended treatment increased pulmonary embolus risk (RR 1.87) and endometrial cancer (years 5–14: 3.1% versus 1.6%).

studies.population: 20 randomized early-breast trials; 21, 457 women overall; ER-positive efficacy analysis 10, 645.
studies.comparison: About 5 years adjuvant tamoxifen versus no tamoxifen.

outcomes.interpretation: Earlier recurrence gains persist after treatment ends; the later near-unity rate ratio is not loss of the prior benefit.
Roughly one-third lower breast-cancer mortality through 15 years; do not label this as overall survival.

limitations: Absolute benefit depends on baseline recurrence risk. Relative effects are not absolute risk reductions.
ER-negative disease showed little or no effect. This historical adjuvant comparison does not quantify metastatic benefit or rank modern endocrine combinations.

studies.population: 12, 894 randomized after 5 years of tamoxifen; breast-cancer efficacy among 6, 846 ER-positive women; harms among all receptor groups.
studies.comparison: Continue to 10 years versus stop at 5 years.

outcomes.interpretation: Overall mortality was reduced in the ER-positive efficacy analysis; these event counts are not a fixed-time survival percentage.

studies.harms: Pulmonary embolus RR 1.87 (95% CI 1.13–3.07); endometrial cancer years 5–14: 3.1% versus 1.6%.
limitations: Benefit became more apparent after year 10. Longer treatment is an individual risk–benefit decision.
Do not conflate efficacy population with all-receptor safety analysis or convert cause-specific mortality into OS.

studies.publication_type: ASCO meeting abstract; not a full-text efficacy report at this source.
studies.population: 6, 953 women: 2, 755 ER-positive and 4, 198 ER-untested, after 5 years tamoxifen.
studies.comparison: Continue to 10 years versus stop at 5 years.

outcomes.interpretation: Overall mortality comparison in this report was not statistically significant; do not present it as a proven OS advantage.

limitations: Includes a large ER-untested population.
Later period subgroup effects and combined ATLAS/aTTom analyses differ from the overall aTTom result. Do not silently substitute a pooled result.
Abstract endometrial-risk confidence interval appears internally inconsistent; no numerical CI reused here.

treatment_rationale.summary: Fulvestrant antagonizes and degrades the oestrogen receptor, providing a different endocrine mechanism from lowering oestrogen production. The initial loading schedule establishes exposure before 28-day maintenance. The NCCP00361 card is monotherapy in a specified post-adjuvant anti-oestrogen setting.
treatment_rationale.setting: Postmenopausal ER-positive locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer.
treatment_rationale.line: Relapse or progression on or after adjuvant anti-oestrogen therapy as specified by NCCP00361.
factors: Confirm prior endocrine exposure, menopausal state and exact indication.
Assess pace and symptoms of disease, performance status and suitability for endocrine treatment.
Reconcile hepatic impairment/current dose and IM bleeding/nerve risk.
Assess whether a separate molecularly selected or CDK4/6 combination plan is intended.
alternatives: A separate fulvestrant combination may be appropriate when its own indication and safety criteria are met; capivasertib/fulvestrant uses 00947.
Other endocrine agents or non-endocrine systemic treatment depend on previous therapy, disease urgency and patient priorities.
treatment_rationale.limitations: EMA broader indications and FALCON endocrine-naive data do not silently broaden this NCCP monotherapy card. Critical visceral disease requires specialist decision-making, not a rule that every visceral metastasis excludes endocrine therapy.

evidence_at_a_glance.trial: CONFIRM dose comparison; FALCON endocrine-naive context
evidence_at_a_glance.population: CONFIRM: postmenopausal ER-positive advanced disease after endocrine therapy. FALCON: postmenopausal HR-positive/HER2-negative endocrine-naive advanced disease.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: CONFIRM: fulvestrant 500 mg versus 250 mg. FALCON: fulvestrant 500 mg versus anastrozole 1 mg.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Keep the populations and comparators separate. NCCP00361 does not acquire endocrine-naive eligibility from FALCON; none of these trials evaluates capivasertib/fulvestrant.

endpoints.interpretation: Numerically longer OS with 500 mg; P=.02 was nominal without multiplicity adjustment.
endpoints.limitations: Historical dose comparison; not proof against modern combinations and not a reason to reverse hepatic-dose adjustment.

endpoints.interpretation: PFS improved in the endocrine-naive population (P=.0486).
endpoints.limitations: Population differs from the specific NCCP00361 indications.

endpoints.analysis_status: Prespecified final OS; 68.0% maturity; descriptive nominal testing
endpoints.limitations: Nonvisceral subgroup HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.60–1.20) was also not significant; do not claim proven subgroup OS benefit.

limitations: Median differences do not estimate one individual’s additional lifespan.
PFS and OS are distinct outcomes.
These monotherapy studies do not quantify modern capivasertib/CDK4/6 combination benefit.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Consider injection-site reactions and neuropathy, bleeding risk with IM administration, hepatic effects, asthenia, flushes and joint/muscle symptoms.

studies.population: 736 postmenopausal women with ER-positive advanced breast cancer after endocrine therapy.
limitations: Final OS testing had no multiplicity adjustment.
Historical dose comparison does not establish superiority over modern combinations.
The 250 mg historical comparator does not override an individual hepatic-dose decision.

studies.population: 462 postmenopausal endocrine-therapy-naive women with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.
limitations: Endocrine-naive population differs from NCCP00361 prior adjuvant anti-oestrogen relapse/progression indications.
Monotherapy trial; does not compare with capivasertib or CDK4/6 combinations.

studies.population: Same 462-patient randomized endocrine-naive population; 314 deaths (68.0%) at 11July 2022 cutoff.
studies.subgroup: Nonvisceral subgroup n 208: HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.60–1.20); not statistically significant. Do not claim a proven subgroup survival advantage.
limitations: Prespecified final OS; descriptive analyses with nominal P values.
Medians are not individual life-expectancy gains. PFS improvement does not establish OS improvement.

renderer_note: Tamoxifen recurrence and breast-cancer-mortality are preserved as exact study outcomes and labelled narrative. They must not be relabelled DFS/OS merely to fit renderer endpoint keys.
